tool_args.old_string: Reasoning models with chain-of-thought (CoT) can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. Detecting this safety commitment point requires monitoring, but a prior question remains unanswered: should a monitoring system read the model's hidden states (HS) or its generated text? We show that this comparison's outcome depends critically on which transformer layer is monitored. Through systematic evaluation across four reasoning models, five layer selection metrics, and seven alternative methods, we find that a biased composite metric masks the HS advantage at 32B scale by selecting shallow layers where representation compression inflates threshold crossings. Principled layer selection recovers significant HS precision gains (+15.4 to +21.9pp, Holm-Bonferroni corrected; 4/4 models pass at corrected layers), though 32B results carry model-specific caveats (position mediation, limited coverage). Encoder quality bounds the advantage: against a stronger 1024-dimensional text encoder, only 1/4 models survives correction. Layer selection sensitivity is the robust methodological finding; the empirical HS advantage is conditional, and current probes characterize the commitment phenomenon rather than constitute production detectors.
tool_args.new_string: Reasoning models with chain-of-thought (CoT) can self-jailbreak: their reasoning traces transition from safe deliberation to committed harmful generation without adversarial input. Detecting the commitment point (CP), the reasoning step after which a model's chain of thought becomes irreversibly committed to an unsafe conclusion, requires monitoring internal representations or generated text. We study four reasoning LLMs on the HarmThoughts safety-probing benchmark and show that the outcome of this comparison depends critically on which transformer layer is monitored. A biased composite metric masks the hidden-state (HS) advantage at 32B scale by selecting shallow layers where representation compression inflates threshold crossings. Principled layer selection recovers significant HS precision gains in three of four models (+19.2 to +21.9pp, Holm-Bonferroni corrected); the fourth model's (R1-32B) advantage is position-mediated (residualized gap below minimum detectable effect). Encoder quality bounds the advantage: against a stronger 1024-dimensional text encoder, only 1/4 models survives correction. Layer selection sensitivity is the robust methodological finding; the empirical HS advantage is conditional, and current probes characterize the commitment phenomenon rather than constitute production detectors.
